sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 93

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 93:1
items.html: Kamatz means the compression of the lights, indicating the aspect of Keter — namely, the ten Sefirot of the head. For since there the screen is in the aspect of a coupling of striking, which is the aspect of opposition to clothing in the vessels, as is known, it is discerned there that the lights are compressed with regard to clothing in the vessels. And the opposite of it is the aspect of 'opening,' for it indicates the aspect of clothing in the vessels — that is, after the coupling of striking made in the Malchut of the head, when by the power of the reflected light rising from the coupling of striking the Malchut spreads from above downward into the ten Sefirot of the body. Then the lights were opened and shine spaciously within the vessels, and hence it is called 'opening.' And all the subject matter is from the aspect of the light of Hochma, for the compression of the screen and its rejection of the upper light operates only on the light of Hochma, since there was no restriction on the Hassadim, as is known. Hence the opening is discerned as the opening of the light of Hochma. (Page 316, Item 47; and Page 314, s.v. 'letters').
